village of Cam Na, near Da Nang in Vietnam. Revulsion over the images fueled
opposition to the war - which dragged on for nearly a decade._

Good morning! **Prem** here, reporting to you from Michigan after a dramatic
evening - where a grueling and eventful Democratic primary campaign came to a
titillating close. I was at the Abdul El-Sayed election party in Detroit,
where the results were not called until after we all had left! On that note…

In today's **' First Draft,'** AIPAC failed in its most expensive undertaking
yet. Plus, alleged abuser **Max Miller** 's appearance on CNN went horribly,
and **Donald Trump 's** agriculture secretary took a victory lap over the
administration depriving families of food.

_DETROIT, Michigan - _$30 million. That's how much the American Israel Public
Affairs Committee spent trying to help Congresswoman Haley Stevens beat the
pro-Palestine Abdul El-Sayed in the Michigan Democratic Senate primary.

And the pro-Israel lobby's election spending - along with several other
moneyed interests that altogether spent a total of $60 million to help Stevens
- failed. Stupendously.

Tuesday night was a long one, as was early Wednesday morning. The primary race
was ultimately much tighter than recent polling had indicated. In the end,
though, El-Sayed pulled it off. NBC News
[called](https://x.com/HenryJGomez/status/2084881876833943965) the race for
El-Sayed just before 2am ET. Other major news organizations followed later
Wednesday morning.**** Mallory McMorrow, who dropped out of the Senate primary
last month, quickly
[endorsed](https://x.com/MalloryMcMorrow/status/2084883047107690766) El-Sayed.

El-Sayed recently
[compared](https://www.politico.com/newsletters/playbook/2026/07/27/put-one-
ogre-on-a-pike-01012505) himself on a call with supporters to **" David"**
fighting **" Goliath," **meaning AIPAC and the establishment.
